# @yagnic/opencode-plugin

The YAGNIC plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). It signs OpenCode in to
your organisation's YAGNIC space and brings in, without any setup, what your
administrator configured for your team: models, tools (MCP servers), rules,
skills and agents. Your own OpenCode configuration always wins: the plugin only
fills in what it lacks.

## Install

Don't install it by hand: it is installed and configured by your YAGNIC site.
Follow its "Get started with OpenCode" page.

## Compatibility

OpenCode **v1** and **v2** (from 2.0.18; tested on 2.2.5). The plugin runs
inside OpenCode's own runtime and has no dependency.

## What it stores on your machine

In OpenCode's data folder (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/<provider>/`, by default
`~/.local/share/opencode/yagnic/`), every file readable by you only (`0600`):

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `client.json` | The OAuth client registration (a client id, no secret). |
| `config.json` | The last configuration received, **without the tools' credentials**, used for 30 days when YAGNIC is unreachable, for the same user only. |
| `identity.json` | Which user each recent access token belongs to, by the token's SHA-256. |
| `rotation.json` | The latest tokens exchanged, so that two OpenCode processes refreshing at once do not sign you out. |
| `skills/`, `rules/` | The skills and rules delivered to you; a skill's scripts (files starting with `#!`) are executable, by you only. |
| `runtimes/` | The `uv` binary that runs Python tools, checked against a pinned SHA-256. |

Your sign-in tokens live in OpenCode's own credential store. **The plugin never
writes tool credentials (personal or shared access tokens) to disk**: it hands
them to OpenCode in memory. A tool run locally receives its token in its
environment, like any MCP server configured by hand. Like any environment variable, it can be
read by the other processes of your user account (`ps eww` on macOS and Linux).

## Your personal access tokens

When a tool needs your own access token (a personal access token of your
issue tracker or code forge, for instance), you type it in OpenCode, never on
the YAGNIC site: run `/connect` and pick the tool, named after it and your
organisation. Until then the tool answers with a message telling you to do
so. The plugin injects the token into the tool without a restart, and tells
YAGNIC only whether the tool works and when the token expires, never the token.

OpenCode keeps that token, like your sign-in tokens, **in clear** in its
database (`opencode.db`, readable by you only), and `opencode auth export`
prints it. Give it a short expiry and the narrowest scopes the tool needs. When
your administrator removes the tool, the token stays in OpenCode until you
remove it (`/connect`, or `opencode auth logout`): revoke it in the tool too.

When a tool signs you in with your own account (OAuth), its tools stay hidden
until you do: run `opencode mcp auth <tool>` (or, in the terminal interface,
type `/mcp` and pick the tool) and sign in in the browser that
opens. Until then, the agent is told which tools wait for your sign-in and
gives you that command, instead of saying the tool does not exist.

## When YAGNIC is unreachable

The plugin re-reads your configuration every minute. If YAGNIC does not answer,
or your session expired, your tools keep working for an hour (option `outage_keep_seconds`), then they
are removed until YAGNIC answers again; your models, rules and skills stay. A
tool that fails meanwhile tells the model that YAGNIC is unreachable. If your
access was revoked, or a tool was removed by your administrator, it goes at
once.
